label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Tolu, I'm the person you're asking for. I wrote JAMB in 2025, scored 251, applied for Medicine and Surgery, and they gave me Biology. I'm in 100L Biology now at a federal uni here in Lagos. So I'll tell you how it really is from inside, not from outside.

**First, how I took it**

The day I saw Biology on that portal, I locked myself in my cousin's room in Surulere and cried. I didn't eat that day. So when you say you've been crying since afternoon, I understand. It's not you being dramatic. You had your mind on one thing and the thing changed.

And it wasn't only me. My mum was still telling people in church that I'm doing Medicine for like two months after. I had to beg her to stop. So if there's pressure from home on top of your own disappointment, I know that one too.

I'm saying all this so you know I'm not one of those people who'll just say "it's fine, accept it, God knows best." It was not fine for me at the beginning. But it got better, and I'll tell you how.

**Can you actually transfer? The honest answer**

Kingsley said transfer is a myth. That's not true. Favour said just read hard and you'll transfer. That's too simple. The truth is in the middle and it's not as sweet as Favour made it sound.

This is what our level adviser told us in my school (and I'm saying MY school, because every school has its own rules):

- You need a CGPA of at least **4.5 out of 5** after 100L to be considered for transfer to MBBS.
- Even if you get 4.5, **there must be space** in Medicine. Making the CGPA doesn't guarantee anything. It just makes you eligible to be considered.
- Last year, she said about **6 people** were moved in from the whole faculty. She thinks **over 40** applied.
- She also said you need to have met the **Medicine cut-off in both JAMB and post-UTME**. So it's not only your 100L result they look at. They check your entry scores too.

So please, I'm not going to tell you that your 268 means you qualify, because I don't know your school's Medicine cut-off or what you scored in post-UTME. You need to check both. 268 alone doesn't tell us anything about transfer eligibility until you compare it to your school's own cut-off for Medicine. If your post-UTME was below the Medicine cut-off, that could block you no matter how well you do in 100L, at least going by how it works in my school.

So yes, transfer is real. People actually get moved. But it is NOT easy, and nobody should accept Biology thinking it's automatic. If you accept with the mindset of "I'll just transfer next year," you're setting yourself up for another heartbreak.

**My own CGPA, since I'm being honest**

My CGPA after first semester is **4.31**. Not 4.5. I'm still trying, second semester is going on, and I haven't given up. But I want you to see that even someone who wanted it badly and is reading isn't automatically there. 4.5 is very high.

The courses in 100L for us are BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST courses. The ones dealing with people are **Physics and Maths**. If you're not strong in those two, start preparing now, whichever way you go. A lot of people who want to transfer lose it in PHY and MTH, not in the Biology courses.

Small practical gist too: lab coat was 6,500 naira, dissecting kit was 9k, and the practical manual is extra. So if you accept, budget for those early.

**Is Biology a bad course?**

No. Biology is not a bad course. I didn't believe that at first because my mind was on Medicine, so anything that wasn't Medicine felt like failure.

But this is what changed it for me. Our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted, lol. I was fine. And that day I realised I actually like this thing. Not "I'm managing it," I actually like it.

I'm enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I expected. There are things in this course that are genuinely interesting, and it's not a dead end. I'm not saying that to make you feel better. I'm saying it because I came in with the same "Biology is consolation prize" mindset and it turned out not to be true for me.

**What about rewriting?**

I won't pretend rewriting is wrong. If you're truly ready, it's a valid choice. But let me tell you about Ifeoma.

Ifeoma was my classmate in secondary school. She got offered Pharmacy and rejected it to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB **two more times** since then. She's still at home. I'm not telling you this to scare you. It's just the side of the story people don't post. Everyone talks about the person who rewrote and got it, nobody talks about the people still waiting.

Favour is right that staying at home is not easy. Seeing your mates go to school while you're at home reading the same JAMB syllabus again can mess with your head. But that doesn't mean rewriting is wrong. It means you should only do it if you're ready for that year, and maybe more than one year, mentally and with support at home.

**What I'd actually tell you to do before your deadline**

1. **Go to the faculty or the Biology department yourself** and ask them the exact transfer rules for YOUR school. What CGPA do they need? Do you need Medicine cut-off in both JAMB and post-UTME? How many people got moved last year, and how many applied? Don't just trust forum people, and that includes me. What I've told you is from my school. Yours might be stricter or easier.

2. **Check the Medicine cut-off for your school** in both JAMB and post-UTME, and compare it to your scores. That one thing will tell you a lot about whether transfer is even on the table for you.

3. **Ask yourself one honest question:** do you want Medicine, or do you want to be "doctor" for your parents and the people around you? I'm not judging. A lot of us have both mixed together. But it matters, because if it's really your own dream, you'll fight for it whichever road you take. If it's more for other people, maybe give Biology a real chance before you decide it's not for you.

4. **If you accept,** go in with two plans at the same time. Plan A: read like your life depends on it, especially PHY and MTH, and aim for the transfer. Plan B: actually pay attention to the course, because you might like it, and if transfer doesn't happen, you're not starting from zero.

5. **If you rewrite,** make sure it's a real decision, not just running from the disappointment. Have a reading plan and talk honestly with your family about what happens if it takes more than one try.

**Last thing**

Whatever you choose, it is not the end of the world. I know it feels like it right now. I promise you it felt like that for me too, crying in that room in Surulere with no food. A year later, I'm here dissecting toads, enjoying genetics, still fighting for my 4.5, and I'm okay. Not perfect, but okay.

You scored 268. You're clearly brilliant. That doesn't disappear because of what the portal says. Take a few days, cry if you need to, then go and get the real information from your school, and make the decision with your eyes open.

If you have more questions about 100L or anything, ask me here. I'll answer.

Amaka
